clue.text: "O _______ " (The 25) Actors have held up tenpin bowlers? What nonsense!

definitions.note: the missing words of a line from The Tempest, the answer to 25

indicators.note: nonsense is words that make no sense in their present order, so the preceding letters must be rearranged

parts.words: Actors have held up tenpin bowlers? What
parts.note: all thirty-three letters of these six words are the raw material

explanation.surface: A sceptic scoffs at the idea of a troupe of actors waiting on a team of ten-pin bowlers.
explanation.walkthrough: Miranda's line in The Tempest is "O brave new world, / That has such people in't!" The whole quotation fills three lights, and the first three words became Huxley's title (see 26).
explanation.definitionFit: Miranda speaks this exclamation on first seeing other humans, so these words complete the quoted line from Shakespeare's play.

clue.text: Wild canaries? I produce more than a pet!

indicators.note: something wild is out of control and disordered, so the letters that follow lose their order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bird keeper boasts of breeding wild canaries, something grander than an ordinary household pet.
explanation.walkthrough: A pet here is a sulk or fit of pique, not an animal: to raise Cain is to make far more fuss than a mere pet.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise Cain is an idiom for causing an angry uproar, a bigger outburst than a passing sulk.

clue.text: Does she take a bow for her Cesario?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a stringed instrument played with a bow
second meaning: the Twelfth Night heroine who goes disguised under the name Cesario

explanation.walkthrough: Taking a bow sounds like an actress at curtain call; here it is the bow of a string instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The heroine of Twelfth Night dresses as a page named Cesario, and the instrument of the same name is bowed.

clue.text: Opus of the blase aerialist?

parts.note: surface reading: a piece of music, perhaps by a circus performer
setter's reading: a trapeze artist casual enough to work with nothing below to catch a fall, split into two words

explanation.walkthrough: Split it as NO NET and it is what a fearless trapeze artist works without; read whole, it is a piece for nine players.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonet is a musical composition written for nine instruments or voices, so it can be an opus.

clue.text: Pendragon in flight from such literary heights

definitions.note: the answer is the word that goes before Heights in the novel's title

indicators.note: one piece sits within the other, as the legendary king is placed inside the word for flight

parts.note: a wing is a flight, as in the wing of a building or an air force unit
Uther Pendragon was King Arthur's father in legend

explanation.surface: A legendary king takes off from some famous literary heights.
explanation.walkthrough: Pendragon is the surname of Uther, Arthur's father. Wuthering Heights is Emily Brontë's novel, so the answer is the kind of heights she wrote about.
explanation.definitionFit: Emily Brontë named her novel's moorland house Wuthering Heights, so this adjective describes those famous literary heights.

clue.text: Elijah and Jeptha are as Brutus is, so one reflected

parts.note: Antony in Julius Caesar says 'I am no orator, as Brutus is'

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror shows things the other way round, so these words are read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Two biblical figures are said to share a quality with Brutus.
explanation.walkthrough: The Brutus line comes from Mark Antony's funeral speech in Julius Caesar. Elijah is Mendelssohn's and Jephtha Handel's.
explanation.definitionFit: Both titles are large-scale sacred works for soloists, choir and orchestra, the form called an oratorio.

clue.text: Composer-king capturing hearts

indicators.note: capturing something means holding it inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: King Lear of Shakespeare's play
H is the abbreviation for hearts in card games

explanation.surface: A royal composer wins over the public's hearts.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen joins definition and wordplay: the composer is one thing, the king another.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Lehár was the Hungarian composer of operettas, most famously The Merry Widow.

clue.text: See 1
The presumption to speak of Jane's skill?

indicators.note: speaking is saying it out loud, so the answer matches what is heard, not what is written

parts.note: Jane Austen's talent as a novelist

explanation.surface: A reader wonders whether it is presumptuous to praise Jane Austen's talent.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostensibility is the quality of seeming so on the face of it, the outward appearance one presumes to be true.

clue.text: King Charles splitting union with King James's supporter

indicators.note: splitting a word means breaking it open so that something can be placed inside

parts.note: taken as written
Carolus Rex, the royal cipher of King Charles

explanation.surface: King Charles is shown dividing the union that his father King James created.
explanation.walkthrough: The two letters are themselves split up: one goes after UNI, the other after the O. James I brought the Scottish unicorn into the royal arms when he united the crowns.
explanation.definitionFit: The unicorn is one of the two heraldic beasts holding up the royal coat of arms, added under James I.

clue.text: See 1
One laughs only if spotted

parts.note: surface reading: someone who laughs only when caught out or noticed
setter's reading: a creature with a spotted coat known for its laughing call

explanation.walkthrough: Spotted means seen in the surface, but it is the coat pattern of the species famous for its cackling cry.
explanation.definitionFit: The spotted hyena of Africa is known as the laughing hyena because of its giggling call.

clue.text: Where Parisians stake their cash? T' heavenly barmaid's holding ours

parts.note: the shortened form of 'the' taken as written

indicators.note: holding something means having it inside, so the goddess's name surrounds the next word

parts.note: Hebe was cupbearer to the Greek gods
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dialect speaker claims the heavenly barmaid is keeping hold of their money.
explanation.walkthrough: Hebe poured nectar for the gods on Olympus, hence a heavenly barmaid.
explanation.definitionFit: La Bourse is the Paris stock exchange, where French investors put their money at risk.

clue.text: Cutbacks writing the end of education?

indicators.note: going backwards means the letters of the cutting word are read from right to left

parts.note: read as 'cut' plus 'backs': to axe is to cut
MS is short for manuscript, a piece of writing

explanation.surface: Spending cuts written up as the death of education.
explanation.walkthrough: Cutbacks reads as one word for budget cuts; split it as 'Cut' plus 'backs'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tests come at the close of a course or a school career, so they can be called its end.

clue.text: Battle for Nile so desperate

indicators.note: something desperate is frantic and in disarray, so the letters before it are thrown about

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A desperate fight for control of the Nile.
explanation.walkthrough: The Nile suggests the naval Battle of the Nile, but the battle wanted is in northern Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Solferino, in 1859, was a bloody clash of the Second Italian War of Independence, prompting the Red Cross.

clue.text: Free entry to good clubs' football fields

indicators.note: making an entry into something means going inside it, so this word goes into the pair that follows

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for good
to rid is to free
irons are a type of golf club

explanation.surface: Good golf clubs get free admission to the football grounds.
explanation.walkthrough: Irons are golf clubs, so the football looks out of place; the definition is American, where the field is marked like a grill.
explanation.definitionFit: A gridiron is an American football field, named for its grid of yard lines.

clue.text: Innocent suspect left 'til wounded internally

indicators.note: internally means on the inside, so the jumbled letters are placed within the opening word

parts.note: to suspect is to guess

indicators.note: something wounded is damaged and out of shape, so the letters before it are jumbled

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for left
taken as written

explanation.surface: An innocent suspect was left alone until he was wounded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Innocent suspect' looks like a phrase, but 'suspect' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone guiltless is free of blame, a direct synonym for being without fault or crime.

clue.text: Eastern logic failing in one epoch

indicators.note: one piece sits within the other, so the scrambled word goes inside the number word

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: something failing is breaking down, so the word before it is disordered

parts.note: taken as written
E is the abbreviation for Eastern

explanation.surface: Eastern reasoning broke down during one historical era.
explanation.walkthrough: E comes first in the clue but goes last in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oligocene is a geological epoch of the Tertiary period, about 34 to 23 million years ago.

clue.text: In pain? Miss Trent's g-going up the wall with this!

definitions.text: going up the wall with this!

indicators.note: in means contained by, so the girl's name goes inside the word for suffering

parts.note: taken as written
Little Nell Trent is the heroine of Dickens's The Old Curiosity Shop
the stammered first letter taken as written

explanation.surface: A pained, stammering Nell is driven up the wall by something.
explanation.walkthrough: The stammer 'g-going' supplies a spare letter while 'going up the wall' still reads as exasperation.
explanation.definitionFit: Wooden panels are fixed to a wall as decorative cladding, so this is what goes up on the wall.

clue.text: The way the Italian book displays some brightness

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
il is Italian for 'the'
B is the abbreviation for book

explanation.surface: An Italian book on the road shows a gleam of brightness.
explanation.definitionFit: The stilb is a unit of luminance, a measure of how bright a surface appears.

clue.text: Basic as stewed eel with bananas

indicators.note: stewed food is cooked into a mush, so the word after it is mixed up

parts.note: taken as written
bananas and mental are both slang for crazy

explanation.surface: A simple dish: stewed eel served with bananas.
explanation.walkthrough: Bananas looks like an ingredient, but it is slang for mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Elemental means fundamental or rudimentary, relating to first principles, so it means basic.

clue.text: Hymn for the next Olympiad

indicators.note: the letters wanted stand in for part of the phrase, lying within the next two words

parts.note: found spanning the two words

explanation.surface: A song is chosen for the coming Olympic Games.
explanation.walkthrough: Hymn is a verb here, meaning to praise.
explanation.definitionFit: To hymn someone is to sing their praises, and to extol is likewise to praise highly.

clue.text: Not locked on this

parts.note: surface reading: describing a door left unsecured
setter's reading: a door closed but not locked is said to be 'on the' something

explanation.walkthrough: A door 'on the latch' is shut but can be opened without a key.
explanation.definitionFit: A latch is a simple fastening bar; a door left on it is closed but not secured with a lock.

clue.text: Dufy, painter or French Liberal

definitions.note: the answer is the painter's first name

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a painter
ou is French for 'or'
L is the abbreviation for Liberal

explanation.surface: Asks whether Dufy was a painter or a French Liberal politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Painter' seems to define Dufy, but it is part of the wordplay; Dufy alone defines his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Raoul Dufy was the French Fauvist painter, so his given name is what the surname points to.

clue.text: Improved recording from recorders in King's Cross?

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the record company sits between the two letters

parts.note: R for Rex, king
EMI is a British record company
a cross is the shape of X

explanation.surface: A better recording made by recorder players at King's Cross, the London railway station.
explanation.walkthrough: King's Cross is a major London station, but here King and Cross are separate pieces either side of the record label.
explanation.definitionFit: A remix is a new version of a recording made by rebalancing or reworking the original tracks.

clue.text: Salt of the Black Mass, say?

indicators.note: say asks you to speak the phrase out loud and hear what it resembles

parts.note: a Black Mass is a ceremony held at night

explanation.surface: Asks about the salt used in a satanic ritual.
explanation.definitionFit: A nitrite is a salt of nitrous acid, as used in curing meat, so it is a chemical salt.

clue.text: What doest Shakespeare's stand-in amanuensis: this work?

definitions.note: Shakespeare's play is the work meant

parts.note: a temp is a temporary secretary
Shakespearean English puts -est on a verb after thou, as in doest

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned question asks what a substitute secretary does in a Shakespearean work.
explanation.walkthrough: Making 'temp' a verb, thou tempest is what a stand-in secretary doest, in Shakespeare's English.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tempest is Shakespeare's late romance set on Prospero's island, so it is the work referred to.

clue.text: Creator of 1 (initialised) should, wandering in a light straight line

definitions.note: the novelist with his middle initial

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the jumbled word goes within the word for light

parts.note: a ley line is a straight alignment of ancient sites

indicators.note: something wandering moves aimlessly, so the word before it loses its order

parts.note: taken as written
lux is Latin for light and a unit of illumination

explanation.surface: Instructions on how a wanderer should drift into a beam of light along a straight path.
explanation.walkthrough: The jumbled letters go between the L and UX. Huxley's novel Brave New World took its title from the line at 1; his middle name was Leonard.
explanation.definitionFit: Aldous Leonard Huxley wrote the dystopian novel Brave New World, published in 1932.
